units.notes: marl, sand, & gravel, up to 25,000 years old

basin & range valley-filling deposit of tufaceous sandstone and siltstone, tuffaceous mudstone, debris flows, marl, and fine-grained quartz sandstone; no tuff samples dated here, but dates obtained elsewhere in northern Utah range between 4 and 14 m.y.; Salt Lake Formation is exposed in an area of about one square mile on the northeast side of Terrace Mountain; dips range up to 45 degrees
exposed 6 miles west of Terrace Mountain; 38 m.y.  Rb-Sr
interbedded thin-bedded fossiliferous limestone and calcareous shale and siltstone. Early Triassic conodonts Ellisonia and Furnishius reported
fossiliferous limestone with light-gray chert; contains hash of disarticulated crinoid, brachiopod, and bryozoan fragments; conodont Merrilina indicates late Permian age
thin- to thick-bedded cherty dolomitic sandstone; tan to dark brown, with interbeds of silty limestone; Murdock Mountain Formation is late Early Permian in age
calcareous siltstone and shale; minor limestone
light-gray sandy dolomite and brown dolomitic sandstone; unfossiliferous
